_: Whole human saliva at ~35 C: 99.5 % water with mucins (MUC5B, MUC7), proteins and salts; shear-thinning and viscoelastic (stringy, spinnbarkeit), an excellent boundary lubricant of soft oral tissue. Built from water.variants.saliva plus research. World lane 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: a free liquid surface; mucin films on tissue follow papillae

n.src: water.variants.saliva: 99.5 % water; no measured value found (GAPS 7)
water.variants.saliva: 99.5 % water; no measured value found (GAPS 7)

absorption.v: clear; water-like absorption (negligible at mm scale in the visible)
absorption.src: GAPS 5 water mu_a < 1 per m in 400-700 nm

scattering_length_mm.src: not found: no scatterers resolved; clear film

density_kg_m3.src: HUMPHREY01: E: recalled (specific gravity 1.002-1.012, standard physiology), not re-read; the Humphrey 2001 abstract gives no numbers

flow_mL_min.src: HUMPHREY01: E: recalled from Humphrey & Williamson 2001, not re-read (the abstract gives no numbers)

daily_L.src: HUMPHREY01: E: recalled from Humphrey & Williamson 2001, not re-read

lubrication.src: BONGAERTS07: E: recalled from Bongaerts 2007 (PDMS-PDMS model contact), not re-read (publisher page refused 11-08): saliva cuts friction ~2 orders

stringiness.v: viscoelastic threads between lips/teeth when the mouth opens (spinnbarkeit); thread length grows with mucin (unstimulated > stimulated)
stringiness.src: STOKES07: E: recalled from Stokes & Davies 2007 (shear-thinning, viscoelastic, G' > G'' at low strain), not re-read

v.film_on_surface: the film's own thickness (layers / film values)

collision_thickness_mm.src: ANON_E solver convention: a liquid has no skin of its own; it keeps a no-penetration boundary at solids

model.v: incompressible: no stiffness ramp; a pressure projection (or weakly compressible SPH with numerical sound speed >= 10x the max flow speed) keeps it out of solids and out of itself
model.src: bulk modulus (water 2.2 GPa: effectively incompressible at body speeds)

boundary_wetting.v: the contact angle per pair (pairs/world.json wetting) sets the meniscus at a solid

restitution.src: RICHARD02 / DEGENNES04: drops stick and spread on wettable solids; bounce only on (super)hydrophobic ones

response_time_ms.src: RICHARD02 tau = 2.6 sqrt(rho R^3/gamma) with rho 1005, gamma 0.0456 N/m

wave_speed_m_s.src: sound ~ water's (CRC; oils ~1450); capillary-wave phase speed sqrt(2 pi gamma/(rho lambda)) at lambda 1 mm

damping_ratio.v: viscous: set by viscosity_mPa_s (no separate damping)

model.src: STOKES07: E: recalled from Stokes & Davies 2007 (shear-thinning, viscoelastic, G' > G'' at low strain), not re-read

elastic_dominant_low_strain.v: G' > G'' at low strain (weak gel)
elastic_dominant_low_strain.src: STOKES07: E: recalled from Stokes & Davies 2007 (shear-thinning, viscoelastic, G' > G'' at low strain), not re-read

relaxation_s.src: not found: an extensional relaxation time for whole saliva (CaBER literature) was not retrieved

note.v: drops and threads: a power-law fluid (n_flow ~0.5-0.8, E) with a small elastic stretch term; films: thin-film lubrication

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) with the values above

stimulated.src: ANON_E: stimulated (parotid-rich) saliva is thinner, more watery (SCHIPPER07 trend)

set.contact.lubrication: lost: friction of soft tissue rises toward the dry value

ERMPS18.cite: Evaluation of salivary surface tension in a cohort of young healthy adults. Eur Rev Med Pharmacol Sci 22 (2018), PMID 29565473 (via GAPS 7)
ERMPS18.lic: terms not stated; numbers used as facts

SCHIPPER07.cite: Schipper RG, Silletti E, Vingerhoeds MH. Arch Oral Biol 52:1114 (2007) (via GAPS 7)

MOUTHMD.cite: The project's research note mouth_teeth_tongue.md D19 / section 10 (saliva film by site, R22; rheology snippets R36)

HUMPHREY01.cite: Humphrey SP, Williamson RT. A review of saliva: normal composition, flow, and function. J Prosthet Dent 85:162-169 (2001). Recalled: unstimulated ~0.3-0.4 mL/min, stimulated ~1-3 mL/min, 0.5-1.5 L/day

BONGAERTS07.cite: Bongaerts JHH, Rossetti D, Stokes JR. The lubricating properties of human whole saliva. Tribol Lett 27:277-287 (2007). Recalled: saliva cuts soft-contact (PDMS) friction by ~2 orders, boundary mu ~0.02

STOKES07.cite: Stokes JR, Davies GA. Viscoelasticity of human whole saliva collected after acid and mechanical stimulation. Biorheology 44:141-160 (2007). Recalled: shear-thinning, elastic (G' > G'' at low strain), long extensional relaxation (spinnbarkeit)

GAPS.cite: Project research note the project's materials research note GAPS_RESEARCH.md (11-07), which carries the primary citations (IAPWS14/08, MAVON97, ELKHYAT04, MOTWANI01, SONNER15, SCHIPPER07, ERMPS18, DAIMON07, POPEFRY97)
GAPS.lic: project record; primary sources' terms listed there

IAPWS.cite: IAPWS releases: Surface Tension of Ordinary Water Substance (2014); Viscosity of Ordinary Water (2008); IAPWS-95 density; thermal conductivity (2011)
IAPWS.lic: freely available releases; numbers used as facts

ANON_E.cite: Estimate made in this lane; the reason is given in each src

RICHARD02.cite: Richard D, Clanet C, Quere D. Contact time of a bouncing drop. Nature 417:811 (2002): tau = 2.6 sqrt(rho R^3 / gamma), independent of impact speed

DEGENNES04.cite: de Gennes P-G, Brochard-Wyart F, Quere D. Capillarity and Wetting Phenomena. Springer (2004): capillary length, Bond number, Tanner spreading

CRC.cite: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (any recent edition): standard property tables for water, ice, air, oils. Values recalled as standard table values, not re-checked line by line this session
CRC.lic: copyright, paywalled; individual physical constants used as facts, no table copied
